experiment: goal-conditioned value head V(z, z_goal) for CEM planning
implementation: tiny_jepa/value_head.py (new); planning_gwmr.py: value_head param added to plan_cem_latent_goal
data: 200 eps x 64 steps MazeWorld, 50/50 random/greedy, 12800 steps, 64 pellets eaten; label = pellet eaten within next 20 steps (4% positive); z_goal per pellet position via build_goal_embedding

value_head.arch: MLP [64, 64, 1] on concat(z, z_goal), sigmoid, BCE
value_head.note: without balanced batches it collapsed to always-negative (0.975 acc, 0.000 pos acc)

planner_eval.protocol: 20 episodes x 64 steps, seeds 5000..5019, true pellet_xy, maze_rollout.npz

diagnostics.note_corr: near-zero corr is EXPECTED for a maze-aware value: Euclidean distance ignores walls; a good V should not track it
diagnostics.V_real_vs_imagined: V(real)=0.393, V(imagined stay)=0.334, V(imagined move)=0.485 - V differentiates imagined futures

honest_verdict: PARTIAL: value head learned a real signal (79% held-out, not a distance proxy) and the planner improved 2x over the previous best latent planner (0.05 -> 0.10), but still below random (0.15) and far below greedy (0.40). Diagnosis: V is a myopic SUCCESS DETECTOR, not a progress guide. Trained on 20-step labels from weak (random/greedy) policies, most maze states are >20 steps from success, so V is flat ~0 across most of the state space and provides no gradient for CEM to follow. This is offline-RL distribution shift: V trained on states visited by weak policies, evaluated on the planner imagined states. The arc stands: encoder geometry OK, metric OK, predictor OK, planner formulation OK - but long-horizon task-aligned value remains the frontier. Next would be TD learning or Monte Carlo returns from stronger policies, i.e., real offline RL, not a supervised classifier.
